title: Frozen v005 and v006 code/outputs equal the hashes in their local manifests (read-only comparison)
C++ exact verifier reproduces python (v006) |S_T| and false-exclusion counts at EVERY energy-level threshold of 1x1 and 2x2, plus E0 and |S_G|; Gray-code incremental energy equals direct energy
Per-state energy: C++ equals frozen v005 python on all 4,096 2x2 states and on 2,002 seeded 3x3 states (incl. all-down and all-up)
3x3 grammar set: brute-force scan of all 16,777,216 states equals python constructive set (v006) and C++ constructive generation (count, id sum, id xor)

3x3 exact scan is complete (2^24 states evaluated by both direct and Gray-code passes), deterministic across 3 repeats, and the accumulated Gray-code drift stays >=10x below the 1e-9 degeneracy tolerance (<=1e-10 of the energy scale)

detail.criterion: drift <= 1e-10 * scale (>=10x below the 1e-9 level-degeneracy tolerance)
detail.amendment_disclosure: The first run applied a 1e-12 relative criterion carried over from the 2x2 comparison; it failed with drift 1.79e-11 because rounding accumulates over 2^24 incremental steps. The criterion was then re-derived from the design (must be well below the degeneracy tolerance) and the test re-run. Target membership uses the direct energies, not the Gray pass, so drift cannot alter any target set.

title: Component costs measured separately (direct energy, grammar scan, incremental energy, constructive generation, memory) and 4x4 exact-verification cost extrapolated as an explicit estimate

costs.memory_note: full verifier stores one double per state (134 MB at 3x3); a streaming variant is required beyond ~N=28
costs.label: component costs, single thread, not a speedup; G_net is not computed in v007

extrapolation_4x4.basis: linear extrapolation of the measured 3x3 Gray-code rate; cost per step also grows with N (O(N)), so this is a LOWER bound; not measured; requires a streaming verifier (storage of 2^40 energies is impossible)
